key_insight: THz time-domain spectroscopy can fingerprint specific grain-boundary defects in organic halide perovskite films and quantify them via defect-related absorption strength.
engineering_relevance: This enables a non-contact, room-temperature, closed-loop diagnostic for defect passivation and quality control in perovskite solar-cell manufacturing.
method: Measure THz spectra (0.3–3.0 THz) of SVE-fabricated perovskite thin films.
Match intrinsic phonon and grain-boundary defect vibrations against a composition-specific THz fingerprint library.
Use oscillator-strength analysis to quantify defect concentration and guide passivation in real time.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the 1.58 THz absorption in MAPbI3 scales linearly with XPS-quantified CH3NH2 defect concentration across multiple perovskite compositions.
watch_item: THz fingerprints may be composition- and fabrication-dependent, so robust deployment will require carefully calibrated libraries and validation across device stacks.
paper_title: Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy as a Universal Defect Fingerprinting Tool for Organic Halide Perovskite Solar Cells
